claims.text: Replacing full thermodynamic integration with an MLP-based perturbation scheme will reduce the computational cost of calculating solid-liquid free energy differences.
An MLP trained exclusively on high-temperature liquid configurations will yield accurate free energy differences for Ta-based refractory HEAs.
MLPs trained only on ground-state crystal data will fail in the liquid phase because of extrapolation errors.
The initial material is a Ta-based refractory HEA with a BCC solid structure and unknown liquid structure and melting properties.
At temperatures above 1500 K, the target alloy exists as a liquid.
The target multicomponent alloy has significant lattice distortion and complex liquid short-range order.
Liquid short-range order and local coordination environments are distinct from those in the BCC solid.
Potentials trained only on crystalline data often represent liquid short-range order and coordination poorly.
EAM potentials fail to capture the complex disordered liquid structure of multicomponent systems.
Lennard-Jones-only simulations have been found unreliable for structural predictions in a multicomponent HEA.
Liquid-phase training avoids the extrapolation errors associated with using Lennard-Jones or ground-state potentials for liquid structures.
Liquid-phase training enables accurate perturbation calculations without the computational cost of full AIMD thermodynamic integration.
The liquid-trained MLP will predict melting temperature and free energy difference within 5% of experiment or a high-fidelity AIMD benchmark.
The ground-state-trained MLP will deviate by more than 10% from the melting or free-energy reference.
Full-phase-space ab initio thermodynamic integration is prohibitively expensive for the target system.
The liquid-trained MLP may fail when the liquid exhibits extreme chemical ordering absent from its training set.
High-temperature thermodynamic predictions may be inaccurate when their underlying databases are incomplete or inaccurate.
High-throughput predictions are often limited to narrow composition ranges.
The applicability of an EAM potential to a refractory HEA at high temperature has not been established.

contradictions.description: The proposed MLP is trained exclusively on liquid configurations and is said to avoid extrapolation, yet the same MLP is used to calculate a solid-liquid free energy difference. Evaluating the BCC solid with no solid configurations in training would itself require extrapolation.
The predicted success criterion is agreement within 5%, while falsification requires an error greater than 10%, leaving outcomes between 5% and 10% neither successful nor falsifying.
